correctness.rationale: For B1=[[0,p],[q,0]], B2=B1^T and a=sqrt(pq), the normalized monodromy Q=exp(B2*tau)exp(B1*tau) is positive definite, det(Q)=1 and tr(Q)=2+4*kappa^2*sinh^2(a*tau). Its eigenvalues equal exp(±2*asinh(kappa*sinh(a*tau))). The resulting exact exponent is strictly decreasing when p != q because H(0)=0 and H''(u)=kappa*(1-kappa^2)*sinh(u)/(1+kappa^2*sinh^2(u))^(3/2)<0. The finite endpoint limits are arithmetic and geometric means of the rates minus recovery, proving the complete all-positive-tau sign cases and exactly one zero in the strict interval. Taylor and large-u expansions prove the two claimed boundary asymptotics, including endpoint equalities and p=q. The included stdlib checker passed 1300 random matrix identities and 260 threshold/monotonicity cases, plus example/asymptotic checks. The finite tests are not substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: The narrowly scoped scientific assertion is a complete explicit all-period stability diagram for the mirrored directed two-group SIS linearization, with strict one-crossing law and asymptotic rates. Examined precedents supply spectral-radius threshold methods and general switching stability principles but not this exact classification. Nonmatching prior-title search alone would not justify this decision; primary statements and hypotheses were compared. Residual broader positive-product equivalence is openly retained.
residual_risks: A hidden exact two-matrix-product identity and monotonicity theorem in the broader positive-systems literature may contain the precise classification; available searching and material inspections reduce but do not eliminate this possibility.

Valdano and related continuous/discrete infection-propagator frameworks may have special-case reductions not explicitly presented in the main text; the mathematical monodromy mechanism itself is established prior art.

value.rationale: Alternating reciprocal directed transmission is a natural smallest-dimensional example separating disease-free thresholds for fast and slow contact switching. Its two frozen states each decay when mu>sqrt(pq), but the joint system invades for fast switching when mu<(p+q)/2. The exact Floquet law, strict sign monotonicity, unique crossing and its two sharp duration asymptotics give a complete, interpretable decision boundary, not merely recomputation of an isolated eigennumber or a textbook numerical exercise. The mathematical value resides in the global classification and mechanism under a clearly limited model, without asserting a full nonlinear epidemiological result.
